summary: John's 9th-great-grandfather; Huguenot shipmaster and pilot of the Gironde from Meschers, Saintonge, who fled to Bristol in 1689 and reached New York by 1700.
bio:
André Lamoureux was, per the Reformed Church of Cozes (the Protestant parish about 8 km inland from Meschers), born 3 Nov and baptized 25 Nov 1663, son of Daniel Lamoureux and Marie Touchay (Garner pp.1, 48; probable identification). He was a 'maistre de nauire... cy-devant de Meche en Xaintonge, pillotte' - a shipmaster and licensed pilot of the dangerous Gironde mouth at Meschers-sur-Gironde. Not from La Rochelle (no record ties him there; the confusion probably comes from the Mersereau in-law Suzanne Doucinet 'de la ville de la Rochelle'). He fled with his family to Bristol in 1689: Judith was baptized there 16 Dec 1689; Jacques, who came from France with them, was buried 19 Mar 1690; a Daniel born 1693 died young; Daniel (John's ancestor) was born 29 Nov 1695. He received denization on 22 Jun 1694 (Shaw p.235; the reports call it naturalization by Act of Parliament). He was in New York by 15 May 1700, and the 1703 census lists 'Andrew Lamarue' in the West Ward. On 4 May 1706 Lord Cornbury ordered 'Andrew L'Amoureux, captain of a merchantman' released from impressment into the Royal Navy.

The printed registers of the French Church of New York record André once in person: on 13 Jan 1703 he signed as 'Andre Lamourau' at the wedding of Daniel Bueau and Ester Gaillard ([R4-S1]). A Suzanne de la Tour, probably his wife, who kept her maiden name in the French manner, was a godmother there in May 1700 ([R4-S1]). The Protestant registers of Cozes, where his 1663 baptism is said to be, are online through the Charente-Maritime archives' Archinoe viewer ('Registres protestants', Cozes listed). Round 4 could not read them because the viewer needs an interactive browser ([R4-S2]). His death is still unknown. The Davenport genealogy notes that he disappears from the records after Cornbury's 1706 order, and that Suzanne was last seen in 1720.
